IMAGE 9:
Shout Your Abortion is also a broad network workmen towards reproductive justice. SYA sprang into existence when founder Amelia Bonow posted about her normal, positive abortion and saw it go viral. People started using #shoutyourabortion to share stories combatting the idea of abortion as something rare and shameful.
“It’s really a collective ecosystem of approaches. We help people build the communities they need, and provide resources for people to own their truth and speak it aloud.” —Erin Jorgensen of SYA
The hashtag became an organization that functions as a network, supporting a diverse array of tactics that all amplify one simple message: ABORTION IS NORMAL
Some of what they do: website shares abortion stories, produce and support events, shop with pro-abortion goods, artist in residence program

IMAGE 6:
The modern era of abortion activism began in 1969 when a group of radical New York feminists — who became known as Redstockings— crashed a hearing on abortion (this hearing was comprised of fourteen men and one nun) and started talking openly about their abortions. Dragging abortion out of the shameful shadows and presenting it as a normal, widespread medical and economic issue swelled the ranks of support for abortion.
“Abortion and birth control can’t be understood separately from housing, wages, health care, policing, racial and social hierarchies, immigration, and environmental health.” —Without Apology
It was a WAVE... but by the time Roe v. Wade made abortion legal in 1973, the argument was based on “choice” and “privacy.” All the power and volume of the original argument was GONE.
IMAGE 7:
This history DISAPPEARED
Radical intersectional feminists fought tooth and nail to redefine abortion as a fundamental right... but with time, the narrative became... The nine progressive white men on the Supreme Court decided of their own accord that it was time to support abortion rights.
This is important because abortion activism is hobbled by the arguments that
“Abortion as a basic right is too radical” “You’ll alienate people “You need to focus on small legal victories”
Which ignore the fact that the radical tactic of treating abortion as something normal, widespread, and practical was exactly what already worked.
Activists today are trying to reconnect abortion with this larger framework of reproductive justice
IMAGE 8:
The term “reproductive justice” was coined in 1994 when a group of Black women organized a full paged ad— signed by 800 Black women— in the Washington Post calling for health care reform.
Reproductive rights+Social justice=Reproductive Justice
in 1997, this group coalesced into SisterSong, a national collective of women of color fighting for reproductive justice. They have trainings and workshops, projects mapping BIPOC birth workers across the south, Artists United for Reproductive Justice, Youth Organizing Council, and a lot more.

IMAGE 4:
The current narrative would have you believe that the Catholic Church always held the firm line that life begins at conception and all abortion is homicide. But for many centuries, they in fact held the Aristotelian view of ENSOULMENT, whereby a human soul develops over time during gestation. In this view, a fetus only becomes human at “quickening,” which happens around the fourth month of pregnancy.
The church never loved abortion, but so long as it happened pre-quickening, it was not considered homicide.
Lemme sum this up: Between the 1200s and 1869*, the Catholic Church allowed abortions into the second trimester.
*except for 1588-1591
IMAGE 5:
The Church’s “all abortion is murder” stance didn’t appear until 1869, when Pope Pius IX realized that contraception was curbing population growth, which meant fewer catholics.
At around the same tie in 1873, the United States went to an extreme of reproductive rights removal with the passage of the Comstack Law.
This law banned all abortion “along with all contraceptives and any information about sex or the process of reproduction... [and gave] the ability to raid any bookstore, medical facility, college, office, or home to eradicate not just contraceptive devices or abortion elixirs, but any notion of contraception or abortion.” From “Without Apology: the Abortion Struggle Now,” by Jenny Brown
All of this was done to prevent “obscenity.”

So if you’ve ever wondered when the US adopted its stance that the best form of sex ed was federally enforced ignorance and the criminalization of support— there is actually a clear answer: 1873!
